body.statement: Using the feasible-frame handle \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{fix}}\), determine the exact value of \(\rho_k(K,R)\) for each fixed \(k\ge2\), where the infimum ranges over every \(p,m,M,s,V\) satisfying \((p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T\), \(M/m=K\), and \(V/s=R\), and every \(P\in\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\). In particular, establish whether every such Gaussian objective satisfies \(\gamma_k(F)\ge k/[1+(k-1)KR]\), or construct a member of this class violating the inequality and derive the corrected fixed-budget frontier.
body.justification: The dimension-free frontier is closed, but exact finite-budget geometry may yield a materially stronger certificate for the small budgets used in practice.
body.gap: The constructed family attains the rational expression in the vanishing-contrast limit, while neither generic weak-submodularity theory nor the current angular comparison proves it is universal.
body.consumer: A fixed-budget trial planner would replace the asymptotic dimension-free certificate by the best possible finite-\(k\) guarantee.
